text.p: LONDON, Feb 12 (LPC) - Syndication of the underwriting phase of the $2.5 billion credit for Russia's Gazprom has raised more than $7.5 billion from the market with one bank still deliberating, a Dresdner Bank official said.
Gazprom is said to be "delighted" by the overwhelming response from the market in the underwriting stage, according to Dr. Bernd Fahrholz, senior general manager at Dresdner Bank.

Banks seeking to join the top underwriting co-arranger tier were asked for commitments of $400 million, while underwriting senior lead managers had to put up $200 million. All banks joining the credit have come in at the $400 million co-arranger level, although with such a large oversubscription drastic scale-backs are inevitable.

The credit, which backs the construction of a gas pipeline from Siberia's Yamal Peninsula to Germany, is priced at 200 bps over LIBOR. It has an eight year tenor with a three year grace period. Dresdner Bank Group is arranging the loan and Dresdner Bank Luxembourg is the syndication and facility agent.
General syndication is anticipated shortly, and may even be launched this week. Already, the arrangers have received more than 50 requests from banks wishing to be invited into general syndication.

Although the pipeline is not expected to be completed before 2002, the deal is not dependent on a revenue stream from the finished project. On completion, the pipeline will be able to carry about 50 billion cubic metres of gas annually.
Gazprom is the world's largest gas producer, accounting for about one quarter of world gas output. This year, it forecasts gas output of 580 billion cubic metres.
